text: saw roustabout wedging a wooden wedge under the PRV lever on Flare Knockout Drum at JORHAT-RIG-04 asset AHWR-50MT-RIG during pressure spike. line pressure was crossing 35 bar and guy tried manually holding it shut so line won't pop. immediately told him to stop work and removed wedge, notified driller.

DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT
During compressor startup at NAHARKATIA-EPS-01 CRUDE-PUMP-02 area, operator engaged manual override on low suction pressure trip switch.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Inadequate troubleshooting procedure and operator non-compliance led to safety interlock bypass (ERP Cause Code: CODE-053).

CORRECTIVE ACTION
Interlock manual bypass was reset immediately and compressor taken offline for assessment.

PREVENTIVE ACTION
Re-train shift personnel on safety system override protocols and enforce strict approval requirements.

DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT
During maintenance activities at SHALMARI-WH-09 flare stack using CRANE-MOB-01, an elevated scaffolding structure partially collapsed.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Improper anchoring of tubular scaffolding and failure to conduct pre-use load verification (ERP Cause Code: CODE-005).

CORRECTIVE ACTION
Work was halted immediately, site cordoned off, and damaged scaffolding dismantled.

PREVENTIVE ACTION
Implement mandatory scaffolding inspection tags signed by certified inspector prior to work at height.

DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT
A contract technician experienced mild dizziness and collapsed while carrying out internal visual inspection inside Separator Boot at DULIAJAN-CW-01 WELLHEAD-04.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Failure to perform continuous atmospheric monitoring and inadequate forced draft ventilation inside vessel (ERP Cause Code: CODE-045).

CORRECTIVE ACTION
Technician extracted safely by standby watcher, given first aid, and referred to hospital for observation.

PREVENTIVE ACTION
Enforce mandatory gas testing log sheets every 30 minutes for all vessel entries.

At 08:30 hrs at BAGHJAN-EPS-03, maintenance crew commenced overhaul on GAS-COMPRESSOR-02 unit prior to formal PTW sign-off by Asset Integrity Manager. The compressor skid was still pressurized at 12 kg/cm2 when fitters started loosening flange bolts on the discharge line. Hydrocarbon gas escaped from the flange joint, triggering local LEL detectors and sounding site ESD alarm. Shift Supervisor immediately isolated the suction manifold valve and evacuated the skid area. Investigation revealed crew acted on verbal instruction from shift contractor without waiting for written permit clearance.

saw mechanical team loosening BOP stack side outlet valve on AHWR-50MT-RIG at BAGHJAN-EPS-03 without bleeding off trapped hydraulic pressure from accumulator unit. hose popped with loud bang and sprayed hydraulic fluid across floor. stopped work instantly and briefed team to check pressure gauge down to zero before unbolting.

dropped 12-inch adjustable spanner from top platform of CRUDE-PUMP-02 at NAHARKATIA-EPS-01 from about 15m height. tool fell right near walkways where floor hand was passing, luckily no hit. tool tethering harness was missing on spanner bag, warned fitter supervisor to use lanyards always.

caught tank cleaning gang entering crude storage tank at KUMCHAI-FIELD-03 LOGISTICS-VEH-05 yard without taking multi-gas detector reading or gas clearance ticket. entry hatch was open and guy was already inside half body with torch. pulled him out right away, called HSE officer for proper gas test.

hydra crane reversing back towards manifold skid at NAHARKATIA-EPS-01 CRUDE-PUMP-02 site without any banksman or reverse alarm sounding. rig assistant was standing in blind spot near rear tyre almost got hit. shouted and stopped driver immediately, instructed toolpusher no crane movement allowed without designated spotter.

At 14:15 hrs at BAGHJAN-EPS-03, mechanical contractor technicians initiated valve replacement on GAS-COMPRESSOR-02 discharge header. The cold work permit had been drafted but lacked final signatures from Site Safety Officer and Production In-charge. While unbolting the 4-inch line, residual condensate drained onto the skid deck, creating a spill hazard. Shift Supervisor noticed unpermitted work during routine rounds and suspended the task immediately. The investigation is pending full crew interviews to establish why work began without permit validation.

At 11:00 hrs at DULIAJAN-CW-01, a pipe-carrier truck loaded with drill collars was being parked near WELLHEAD-04. The side stakes on the truck bed were not locked in place and web straps were completely loose. As the vehicle turned onto the gravel access path, two 6-inch drill pipes rolled off the bed onto the ground adjacent to the wellhead flowline. Driver failed to perform pre-transit load checks prior to moving from pipe yard. No injuries occurred, but transport operations were halted for load securement retraining.

DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT
Operator applied a software override on Basic Process Control System (BPCS) liquid level trip during mud circulation startup on MORAN-GGS-02 MUD-TANK-01.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Incomplete pre-startup safety review and bypass of override authorization process (ERP Cause Code: CODE-002).

CORRECTIVE ACTION
BPCS override was removed immediately and mud tank level instrument re-calibrated.

PREVENTIVE ACTION
Lock BPCS trip override permissions to Operations Manager access level only.

synthetic webbing sling snapped during lifting of BOP stack module using CRANE-MOB-01 at SHALMARI-WH-09. load dropped about 1 foot back onto timber mats with heavy thud. inspected sling after incident and found severe tears on edge which was hidden under dirty grease, rigger failed to check sling condition before hook up.

DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT
A derrickman lost balance and fell from monkey board level on BAGHJAN-EPS-03 GAS-COMPRESSOR-02 rig structure, arrested by inertia reel.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Lack of conclusive evidence regarding full body harness attachment point status prior to fall (ERP Cause Code: CODE-057).

CORRECTIVE ACTION
Derrickman lowered safely to drill floor and work suspended for safety equipment inspection.

PREVENTIVE ACTION
Replace standard lanyards with dual tail self-retracting lifelines across all active rigs.

At 09:45 hrs at SHALMARI-WH-09, a maintenance worker entered the primary separator vessel connected to CRANE-MOB-01 maintenance scope for internal scale removal. The vessel had been isolated but nitrogen purging had not been followed by fresh air ventilation, leaving an oxygen-deficient atmosphere inside. Within two minutes of entry, worker lost consciousness near the internal baffle plate. Standby rescue team deployed emergency air supply and retrieved worker within four minutes. Worker was resuscitated at site medical centre and evacuated to regional hospital.

fitter opening flange on live crude transfer line near DULIAJAN-CW-01 WELLHEAD-04 without isolation lock or bleed valve check. line was under 8 bar residual head and sprayed crude on operator boots. stopped job immediately, locked out isolation gate valve, applied LOTO tag before clearing line.

At 03:30 hrs at JORHAT-RIG-04 AHWR-50MT-RIG, instrument technician disabled IR flame detector and toxic gas sensor on main mud tank deck during maintenance. The safety system inhibit was performed directly at local control panel without issuing a Management of Change or bypass permit. Shortly after, a minor gas release from mud degasser line went undetected by automated alarms until manual operator noticed H2S odor. Emergency shut-down valve was manually actuated from Doghouse. Investigation confirmed safety barrier failure due to unauthorized isolation of critical F&G detectors.

electrician opened 415V breaker panel on GAS-COMPRESSOR-02 skid at BAGHJAN-EPS-03 using screwdriver while panel was live and exposed busbars were energized. no rubber gloves or arc flash suit worn, insulated tools not used. shouted to stop work, isolated main MCC feeder switch before letting electrician touch panel.

logistics driver transporting separator fittings to DIGBOI-STATION-01 SEPARATOR-SKID-03 was found sleeping at wheel while engine running at loading bay. shift was driver's 3rd consecutive 12-hour night duty without mandatory rest period. stopped vehicle engine, pulled key out, reported to transport supervisor for driver relief.

DESCRIPTION OF THE INCIDENT
Hot work welder struck an arc near open oily water drain trench at DULIAJAN-CW-01 WELLHEAD-04 during structural repair.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS
Failure to cover open drains within 15-meter radius and inadequate gas monitoring prior to spark generation (ERP Cause Code: CODE-031).

CORRECTIVE ACTION
Welding ceased immediately, flash fire extinguished with dry chemical powder, trench sealed with fire retardant tarpaulin.

PREVENTIVE ACTION
Mandatory fire watcher presence and drain sealing verification prior to hot work permit signing.
